narrative:
Based on the information available, the system has assessed that you have a 66% chance of failing your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that triggers the requirement to take remedial courses. This decision is meant to support your academic success, not to penalise you.

The single most influential factor in this assessment is your history of past class failures. Unlike students who are not required to take remedial courses, who on average have no prior failures, you have already failed one class. This strongly pushes the prediction toward failing, and it carries far more weight than any other factor considered.

Two other factors were also taken into account, though their influence was considerably smaller. Encouragingly, your desire to pursue higher education works in your favour, nudging the prediction slightly toward passing. This ambition is a genuine strength and something you should hold onto. Additionally, having very little free time after school also works slightly in your favour, as it may reflect a more focused daily routine — though this effect is also modest.

It is important to note that your sex, age, and health status played no role in this decision whatsoever.

Given all of this, the most important step you can take right now is to engage fully with the remedial courses being offered to you. Your motivation to continue into higher education shows you have the drive to succeed. Use that ambition to commit to the additional support, address the academic gaps that led to your previous failure, and give yourself the best possible chance of passing your final year.

Protected attributes sex, age and health were not used to make the machine prediction.
